subject: Manual cleaning of GGIR part 4 output

messages.author: 2b23763e80756a9d
messages.subject: Manual cleaning of GGIR part 4 output
parts:
Hello,

We have processed our actigraphy data, mainly focusing on sleep analysis. Our participants completed a sleep diary to complement the actigrpahy data. We have processed the data so that GGIR uses the sleep diary were present, if not, to implement its algorithm if the data is realiable, therefore we have been using the _full.csv when cleaningcode = 0 and 1. 

We have manually cleaned this data, where there was a discrepancy between the sleep diary and GGIR sleep onset of >30 minutes. Additionally, we have visually inspected those cases where the sleep diary was missing and GGIR has used its own algorithm. We have made some adjustments and manual changes to the sleep onset and wake up times in some of our rows of data. Because of this, GGIR's SleepDurationinspt value is now off. We were wondering if it is possible to re process the data, using the an updated advance sleep log with the sleep diary and our manually cleaned sleep variables to inform actigraphy, and thus obtain new accurate measures of SleepDurationinspt and waso. Is this common practice when manually cleaning actigraphy data? If so, would this be the correct approach? 

Thanks a lot in advance for any guidance!

Best wishes,
Pilar

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Manual cleaning of GGIR part 4 output
parts:
Hello Pilar,

Did you consider using the sleep estimates stored in part 5 output? They reflect sleep estimates guided by sleeplog, if sleeplog present for a certain night, or sleep estimates guided by the build-in algorithm if sleeplog is not present for that night.  An additional advantage of the part 5 output is that this directly excludes invalid days, in contrast to the part4 _full report, which does not offer any data cleaning. In part 5 you may want to focus on timewindow = "WW" or "OO" as those reflect the full SPT window, in contrast to "MM" which accumulates sleep per calendar day.

What you could indeed do is:
  • Process the data for the first time as you have done.
  • Correct or impute the sleep log based on your observations.
  • Consider the data_cleaning_file parameter to skip specific nights or days in part 4 and 5.
  • Reprocess part 4 and 5 with the new sleep log and optionally data_cleaning_file parameter.

Does this address your needs?

If not, it would be helpful to aim for a situation where GGIR can help you do most of the work to avoid that you and other GGIR users end up doing a lot of custom data handling outside GGIR which introduces more work for everyone and higher risk for errors and inconsistencies between studies. So even if you use a different strategy it would be good to hear about it.

Best wishes,

Vincent
